\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{লালনপালন} (lālônpālôn)}{লালনপালন (lālônpālôn)}]{\bn{লালনপালন} (lālônpālôn) — upbringing; raising (a child)}

\label{lesson:BN-C486-lalonpalon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a baby, then the Bengali for a cradle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{লালনপালন}}
\textbf{\bn{লালনপালন}} — \emph{lālônpālôn} — \textquotedblleft{}upbringing; raising (a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাবার} \bn{মৃত্যুর} \bn{পরে} \bn{মামা} \bn{অরুণের} \bn{লালনপালন} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bābār mrityur pôre māmā ôruner lālônpālôn kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After his father's death, Arun's uncle brought him up.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{লালনপালন}} (\emph{lālônpālôn}) pairs Sanskrit \emph{lālana}, \textquotedblleft{}caressing, fondling\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{pālana}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, nourishing\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams); \bn{পালা} (taught), to rear, is from the second.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lālônpālôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lālônpālôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bābār mrityur pôre māmā ôruner lālônpālôn kôrlen.} — After his father's death, Arun's uncle brought him up.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a baby, then the Bengali for a cradle, then say \emph{lālônpālôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{লালনপালন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Upbringing; raising (a child)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া} (prôshrôy deoyā)}{প্রশ্রয় দেওয়া (prôshrôy deoyā)}]{\bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া} (prôshrôy deoyā) — to indulge; to spoil (a child)}

\label{lesson:BN-C486-proshroy-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a cradle, then the Bengali for upbringing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{prôshrôy deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to indulge; to spoil (a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দিদিমা} \bn{সবসময়} \bn{নাতিকে} \bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{didimā sôbsômôy nātike prôshrôy den.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother always indulges her grandson.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{নাতনিকে} \bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দিলেন}, \emph{tini nātnike prôshrôy dilen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রশ্রয়} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{prôshrôy deoyā}) is Sanskrit \emph{praśraya}, \textquotedblleft{}leaning on, a resting place\textquotedblright{}, and also affection (Monier-Williams); Bengali uses it for indulgence, a sense the dictionary does not give, with \emph{deoyā}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6141): to give a child something to lean on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôshrôy deoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{didimā sôbsômôy nātike prôshrôy den.} — Grandmother always indulges her grandson.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a cradle, then the Bengali for upbringing, then say \emph{prôshrôy deoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{চোষা} (choshā)}{চোষা (choshā)}]{\bn{চোষা} (choshā) — to suck}

\label{lesson:BN-C486-chosha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for upbringing, then the Bengali for to spoil (a child).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{চোষা}}
\textbf{\bn{চোষা}} — \emph{choshā} — \textquotedblleft{}to suck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাচ্চাটা} \bn{বোতল} \bn{থেকে} \bn{দুধ} \bn{চুষে} \bn{খাচ্ছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāchchāṭā botôl theke dudh chushe khāchchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The baby is sucking milk from its bottle.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{শিশু} \bn{বোতল} \bn{থেকে} \bn{দুধ} \bn{চুষল}, \emph{sei shishu botôl theke dudh chushlô}.

The stem vowel rises in the verb forms: \bn{চুষি}, I suck; \bn{চুষল}, sucked.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{চোষা}} (\emph{choshā}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{cūṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}sucks\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4898, which lists Bengali \emph{cusā}, \textquotedblleft{}to suck\textquotedblright{}); the forms \bn{চুষি} and \bn{চুষছে} keep the old u.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{choshā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāchchāṭā botôl theke dudh chushe khāchchhe.} — The baby is sucking milk from its bottle.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for upbringing, then the Bengali for to spoil (a child), then say \emph{choshā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো} (ghum pāṛāno)}{ঘুম পাড়ানো (ghum pāṛāno)}]{\bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো} (ghum pāṛāno) — to put to sleep (a child)}

\label{lesson:BN-C486-ghum-parano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to spoil (a child), then the Bengali for to suck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো}} — \emph{ghum pāṛāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to put to sleep (a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাবা} \bn{গান} \bn{গেয়ে} \bn{মেয়েকে} \bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ালেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bābā gān geye meyeke ghum pāṛālen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father sang his daughter to sleep.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{শিশুকে} \bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ালেন}, \emph{tini shishuke ghum pāṛālen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঘুম} \bn{পাড়ানো}} (\emph{ghum pāṛāno}) is \bn{ঘুম}, sleep, with \emph{pāṛāno}, \textquotedblleft{}to lay down\textquotedblright{}, from the verb CDIAL lists for Bengali as felling and laying down, under Sanskrit \emph{pātayati} (CDIAL 8053).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেওয়া} (hāmāguṛi deoyā)}{হামাগুড়ি দেওয়া (hāmāguṛi deoyā)}]{\bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেওয়া} (hāmāguṛi deoyā) — to crawl (on all fours)}

\label{lesson:BN-C486-hamaguri-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to suck, then the Bengali for to put to sleep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{hāmāguṛi deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crawl (on all fours)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{ভাইঝি} \bn{এখন} \bn{হামাগুড়ি} \bn{দেয়।}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmār bhāijhi ekhôn hāmāguṛi dey.}

\begin{quote}
My niece crawls now.

\end{cousinweb}
